subject: Post-call exec recap: Redwood x AuroraMed - exec summary & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chris Walker <chris.walker@auroramed.com>, Samantha Green <samantha.green@auroramed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call exec recap: Redwood x AuroraMed - exec summary & next steps

Hi Chris / Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation with the exec team. Below is a short recap for your leadership and the next steps we discussed. Let me know if I missed anything.

High-level outcome: AuroraMed is looking to reduce inference latency for clinician-facing note generation (target P95 < 150ms) while lowering per-token cost and ensuring PHI never leaves your VPC. You're evaluating Redwood to provide a production-grade inference layer (private deployment) with predictable SLAs and clear cost controls.

Key pain points discussed:
- Latency variability on current hosted model endpoints causing UI jitter for clinicians.
- High per-token costs at current scale (est. ~2M tokens/day) impacting unit economics.
- Regulatory requirement: PHI must remain in controlled network; audit logs + KMS integration required.

Business goals & success metrics:
- Pilot (8 weeks) to validate P95 latency < 150ms for the generation flow and average token cost reduction >= 30%.
- Security/compliance sign-off: SOC 2 evidence + KMS/HSM integration completed before production rollout.
- Procurement path clarified: security review -> SOW -> PO -> pilot start.

Risks & escalation items we flagged:
- Data residency/audit log retention policy — legal and infosec need confirmation on retention windows.
- Timeline sensitivity: AuroraMed wants pilot in Q3; procurement timeline may push start date.

Who we heard as decision-makers / sponsors:
- Chris Walker, CTO (technical champion)
- Samantha Green, Head of AI (product/ML sponsor)
- Dr. Elena Morales, COO (executive sponsor — business outcomes / budget)

Next steps (action owners & timing):
1) Redwood to share a one-page technical plan + draft SOW (attached). — Marissa / today EOD.
2) AuroraMed to share procurement contacts and any standard contract redlines. — Chris / by Fri 3/19.
3) Security questionnaire kickoff (Redwood to provide initial SOC2 folder + KMS integration notes). — Laura to lead / next Tue 3/23.
4) Align on pilot success metrics and test plan. — joint session (30m) to schedule for week of 3/29.

Attachments: Aurora_Redwood_MA-Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal summary), SOW-draft.docx (working SOW).

Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. I reviewed the draft SOW and added a couple of lines around audit-log retention windows and KMS key rotation frequency.

I can own the security kickoff next Tue. I'll bring the SOC2 bundle and a short note on our KMS/HSM integration pattern.

One ask for Chris/Samantha: can you confirm whether AuroraMed requires a dedicated VPC endpoint or if a customer-managed subnet in our private deployment is acceptable? That will influence the infra checklist in the SOW.
